_zone.name: Ronda
_zone.description: A white town split in two by El Tajo, a 100-metre gorge spanned by the Puente Nuevo. The birthplace of modern bullfighting, with a Nasrid old town, Arab baths and vineyards in the Serranía.

puente-nuevo.name: Puente Nuevo
puente-nuevo.description: Ronda's icon: an 18th-century stone bridge crossing El Tajo nearly 100 metres up, joining the new town and the old.
puente-nuevo.short_tip: Walk across and peer over its balconies. The interpretation centre is inside.

tajo.name: El Tajo Gorge
tajo.description: A gorge up to 100 metres deep carved by the Guadalevín river, splitting the town in two. Admire it from bridges, viewpoints and trails.
tajo.short_tip: To see it from below, walk down the Camino de los Molinos.

mirador-camino-molinos.name: Puente Nuevo Viewpoint (Camino de los Molinos)
mirador-camino-molinos.description: From below, the Molinos path gives the most famous view of the Puente Nuevo, with the sheer gorge and the waterfall at its feet.
mirador-camino-molinos.short_tip: About 20 minutes down from Plaza de María Auxiliadora. The climb back is tough.

centro-interpretacion-puente.name: Puente Nuevo Interpretation Centre
centro-interpretacion-puente.description: It occupies the chamber inside the central arch, once used as a prison, and explains how the bridge was built in the 18th century.
centro-interpretacion-puente.short_tip: A short visit. Included in the town's tourist pass.

plaza-toros.name: Ronda Bullring
plaza-toros.description: Built in 1785, one of Spain's oldest bullrings and the cradle of bullfighting on foot. Visit the arena, pens, stables and bullfighting museum.
plaza-toros.short_tip: With audio guide, €12. The only bullfight is at the Feria Goyesca in September.

casa-rey-moro.name: House of the Moorish King: Gardens and Mine
casa-rey-moro.description: Early-20th-century terraced gardens and a Nasrid water mine carved into the rock, with stairs leading down to the river.
casa-rey-moro.short_tip: Going down is easy; climbing the mine's steps, less so. Wear comfortable shoes.

banos-arabes.name: Arab Baths
banos-arabes.description: The best-preserved Arab baths in the Iberian Peninsula, from the 13th and 14th centuries, with star-shaped skylight vaults by the river.
banos-arabes.short_tip: Free on Tuesday afternoons. A short film explains how they worked.

palacio-mondragon.name: Mondragón Palace
palacio-mondragon.description: A palace of Nasrid origin remodelled in the Renaissance, with Mudéjar courtyards and gardens hanging over El Tajo. Home to the Municipal Museum.
palacio-mondragon.short_tip: Don't miss the viewpoint garden, looking over the Serranía.

santa-maria-mayor.name: Church of Santa María la Mayor
santa-maria-mayor.description: Built on the site of the main mosque, whose mihrab arch survives, it blends Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque styles.
santa-maria-mayor.short_tip: Audio guide included. It's on Plaza Duquesa de Parcent.

museo-lara.name: Lara Museum
museo-lara.description: A vast private collection in an 18th-century palace: clocks, weapons, fans, cinema, archaeology and rooms on the Inquisition and witchcraft.
museo-lara.short_tip: There's a lot to see: allow at least an hour and a half.

museo-joaquin-peinado.name: Joaquín Peinado Museum
museo-joaquin-peinado.description: In the Palace of the Marquises of Moctezuma, it gathers the work of this Ronda-born painter of the School of Paris, a friend of Picasso.
museo-joaquin-peinado.short_tip: Free on Tuesdays from 3 to 5 pm. Closed on Sundays.

casa-gigante.name: House of the Giant
casa-gigante.description: A 14th-century Nasrid palace-house, one of the few homes of that era to survive, with carved plasterwork and a patio with a pool.
casa-gigante.short_tip: A short visit. Included in the town's tourist pass.

casa-don-bosco.name: Don Bosco House Museum
casa-don-bosco.description: An early-20th-century Modernist house with period furniture and a garden hanging over El Tajo, looking onto the Puente Nuevo.
casa-don-bosco.short_tip: The garden is the highlight: a view of the bridge with few people.

espiritu-santo.name: Church of the Holy Spirit
espiritu-santo.description: A late-15th-century fortress-church built after the Christian conquest beside the town walls, in the San Francisco quarter.

cueva-pileta.name: Cueva de la Pileta
cueva-pileta.description: A cave with prehistoric paintings over 20,000 years old, horses, fish and symbols, visited by the light of hand-held lamps only.
cueva-pileta.short_tip: Guided visits in groups of 15, booking required. 22 km from Ronda, near Benaoján.

reservatauro.name: Reservatauro
reservatauro.description: A fighting-bull ranch in the Serranía: see the animals in their pastures and learn how they are raised.

puente-viejo.name: Puente Viejo
puente-viejo.description: A single-arch bridge from 1616 over the Guadalevín, with views of El Tajo and the Arab Baths.
puente-viejo.short_tip: Combine it with the Arab Baths and the Roman Bridge: they're side by side.

puente-romano.name: Roman Bridge (San Miguel)
puente-romano.description: The lowest of Ronda's three bridges, medieval in origin despite its name, at the entrance to the Arab Baths.
puente-romano.short_tip: From here you can see the Puente Viejo above.

alameda-tajo.name: Alameda del Tajo
alameda-tajo.description: A 19th-century park on the edge of the cliff, with balconies jutting out over the Serranía, like the famous Balcón del Coño.
alameda-tajo.short_tip: Look for the overhanging balcony: vertigo guaranteed.

mirador-aldehuela.name: Aldehuela Viewpoint
mirador-aldehuela.description: A viewpoint beside the Puente Nuevo, named after its architect, with one of the closest views of the gorge and the bridge.
mirador-aldehuela.short_tip: Good photos early in the morning, before the tour groups arrive.

jardines-cuenca.name: Cuenca Gardens
jardines-cuenca.description: Terraced gardens hanging over El Tajo, with roses and views of the Puente Nuevo and the Puente Viejo.

paseo-blas-infante.name: Paseo de Blas Infante
paseo-blas-infante.description: A promenade beside the Parador with viewpoints over El Tajo and the Serranía, continuing along the Paseo de los Ingleses.
paseo-blas-infante.short_tip: At sunset the valley turns orange.

puerta-almocabar.name: Almocábar Gate
puerta-almocabar.description: The main gate of the 13th-century Nasrid walls, beside the Carlos V gate, which led into the town from the south.
puerta-almocabar.short_tip: From here you can see much of the town walls.

plaza-duquesa-parcent.name: Plaza Duquesa de Parcent
plaza-duquesa-parcent.description: The main square of the old town, surrounded by convents, the Town Hall and the church of Santa María la Mayor.
plaza-duquesa-parcent.short_tip: A quiet spot with shaded benches.

plaza-socorro.name: Plaza del Socorro
plaza-socorro.description: The heart of the new town, with the Socorro church and the building where Andalusia's flag and coat of arms were adopted in 1918.
plaza-socorro.short_tip: Lined with bars and shops, five minutes from the Puente Nuevo.

virgen-paz.name: Sanctuary of the Virgen de la Paz
virgen-paz.description: An 18th-century Baroque church where Ronda's patron saint is venerated.

convento-merced.name: Convent of La Merced
convento-merced.description: A convent of Discalced Carmelite nuns that keeps the relic of Saint Teresa of Ávila's hand. The nuns sell homemade sweets.
convento-merced.short_tip: Buy the sweets through the turning window, in the morning and late afternoon.
